key_insight: CLIMB shows that diagnosing co-occurring conditions is much harder than single-diagnosis cases, and models often anchor on the first likely hypothesis instead of recovering the full set.
clinical_relevance: For multimorbidity, asking more questions alone may not improve diagnosis unless the system can actively manage multiple competing conditions at once.
method: Built CLIMB, a benchmark where a doctor model interviews a simulated patient to identify a ground-truth set of co-occurring conditions.
Synthesized cases from clinical decision algorithms and diagnostic datasets to ground presentations in structured clinical knowledge.
Evaluated six frontier and open models on multi-turn, multi-label diagnosis and compared performance with full-record and controlled experiments.
evidence_signal: Across six models, none recovered the exact condition set in more than 10% of interactive cases, and performance dropped further with interaction.
watch_item: The benchmark uses synthesized cases, so real-world deployment still needs validation on noisy, heterogeneous clinical encounters.
paper_title: CLIMB: A Clinical Multimorbidity Benchmark for Diagnosing Co-occurring Conditions through Multiturn Conversations
